angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 380,548 km at 27.15 pc = 0.19 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 36.8291 +/- 0.0176 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 27.15 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.547 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Fridlund et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-776 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..12F/abstract): 380,548 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.542 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Fridlund et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-776 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..12F/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3725 +/- 60 K from Fridlund et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-776 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..12F/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Fridlund et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-776 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..12F/abstract)

ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-776 (pscomppars): age 6.1 Gyr, from Fridlund et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...684A..12F/abstract)
